clue.text: A generous poacher might reveal his secret

definitions.meaning: a poacher takes game birds and animals; a generous one would hand his game over to others
to let slip something that was meant to stay hidden

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to betray a plan unintentionally, and literally describes a poacher handing out his game.

clue.text: Worry follows one in medal business that's successful

indicators.note: the worry comes after the medal-and-one piece in the answer
the word for one sits inside the word for the medal

parts.note: gong is informal British slang for a medal or award
I is the Roman numeral for one
a concern is a worry

explanation.surface: An anxious medal winner turns out to run a thriving firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a profitable enterprise that keeps trading.

clue.text: A picky eater, say, in the camper

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a camper is a camper van, so VAN
EG (for example) is what say means

explanation.surface: Someone fussy about food is travelling in a campervan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is only a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refuses all animal products is selective about food, a picky eater in the setter's teasing sense.

clue.text: Document needed for call to action

parts.note: to call someone something is to give them a title or name
a deed is an action

explanation.surface: Some paperwork is required in response to a rallying cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal paper proving ownership of property.

clue.text: A barrier to audience participation

parts.note: audience is read as hearing: an item that blocks sound entering one's hearing

explanation.definitionFit: A plug worn in the ear keeps noise out, so it stops a listener taking part as a hearer.

clue.text: Leave a group working

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians for instance
on means operating or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A musical group is told it may go while still performing.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or quit, synonymous with leave.

clue.text: Went inside to hear introduction

indicators.note: the clue asks us to listen to the word for went inside spoken quickly

parts.note: entered means went inside

explanation.surface: Someone walked in to listen to an opening piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, the past tense for 'went inside' slurs toward the two-syllable noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is a way in, a first admission or debut, much like an introduction.

clue.text: Speculative new grid on order

indicators.note: the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: An untested new layout has been ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder: NEW, GRID and ON together are rearranged, with 'order' signalling it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wondering is musing or pondering, adjectivally the same as speculating.

clue.text: Acquired following for fashionable bar

indicators.note: the word for acquired comes after the word for fashionable

parts.note: in means in fashion
got means acquired

explanation.surface: Someone obtained a following for a trendy drinking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but means a block of metal; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast block of gold or other metal, a bar.

clue.text: Cringe at drunk showing response

indicators.note: being drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk person's behaviour makes someone wince in reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Reacting is responding, so it means displaying a response.

clue.text: The place to kiss and make up?

definitions.text: The place to kiss and make up?

parts.words: The place to kiss and make up?
parts.note: kiss and make up usually means reconcile; here a famous stone kissed to gain the gift of fluent invented talk

explanation.definitionFit: Kissing this stone at Blarney Castle in Ireland is said to give the gift of the gab, the knack of making things up.

clue.text: Well-bred chap goes to fish

parts.note: a gent is a chap, a man
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A refined man goes fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means refined and polite, as from a good family.

clue.text: Teetotal prisoner's locked up here for battery

parts.note: dry means abstaining from alcohol
a cell is where a prisoner is kept

explanation.surface: A sober inmate is confined in jail with his weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry cell is a battery using paste rather than liquid electrolyte.

clue.text: Charge nothing up front to make a speech

indicators.note: the letter for nothing goes before the word for charge

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A speaker waives the fee in advance before addressing a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal address.

clue.text: Slide along the road to penal reform after a question and answer

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the earlier three letters

parts.note: question gives QU

indicators.note: reform signals the letters of penal being remade into another shape

explanation.surface: A traffic offence is examined in a question-and-answer session about prison reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' turns PENAL into PLANE; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaplaning is when a vehicle skids on surface water, sliding over the road.

clue.text: Boatman doing role play

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are moved about freely

explanation.surface: An actor takes on the part of a boatman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier steers a gondola in Venice, so he is a boatman.

clue.text: An empty radio station might be difficult for a thief

definitions.text: An empty radio station might be
definitions.meaning: a station with no one at the microphone is not broadcasting
a thief would struggle to steal from thin air, nothing tangible to lift

explanation.definitionFit: Off the air means not broadcasting; literally, taking something from the air would be hard for any robber.

clue.text: Rule change due to pact?

indicators.note: change tells us to shift the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A government is replaced because of an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' does double duty in the &lit reading: the whole clue describes the answer while its anagram is signalled by 'change'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'etat is a sudden seizure of government, a change of rule.

clue.text: Musician's instruction to play lot more

indicators.note: play invites the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer is told to play much more.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremolo is a direction in a score to play with rapid repeated notes.

clue.text: A thief is partial to a hot drink!

definitions.meaning: Cockney rhyming slang for a robber
partial here means forming part of, a piece of a cuppa

explanation.definitionFit: Tea leaf is London rhyming slang for thief, and a tea leaf is literally part of a brew.

clue.text: Smoky atmosphere oddly used for composition

parts.note: a fug is a stuffy, smoky atmosphere

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and other odd-placed letters of the word

explanation.surface: A smoky atmosphere was strangely used for writing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes U and E from 'used'; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugue is a contrapuntal musical piece.

clue.text: Restore material with delicate fabric

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
lace is a fine openwork textile

explanation.surface: Fabric is mended using fine lace.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace is to put back, the same as restoring.

clue.text: Name given to a canvas that's put up

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sail is made of canvas

explanation.surface: A title is given to a painting that is hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns SAIL into LIAS; 'given to' and 'that's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed name.

clue.text: Sticks to a present in case of disruptions

indicators.note: the word for present sits inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to a gift through times of upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives D and S, the first and last letters of 'disruptions'; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Adheres means clings, as glue sticks.

clue.text: Rule of wet weather, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for wet weather is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A spell of rain sounds like it is ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is the period or exercise of royal rule.

clue.text: Lawyers object with one voice

parts.note: the Bar is the collective term for barristers
it is a pronoun for an object

explanation.surface: Lawyers raise an objection in unison.
explanation.definitionFit: Baritone is a male singing voice between tenor and bass.

clue.text: Spanish friend French friend shot

parts.note: ami is French for friend
a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: A Spaniard's friend and a Frenchman's friend were shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed directly from the Spanish word for a pal or companion, used in English for a comrade.

clue.text: Where journalists get egg on pears, perhaps

parts.note: to press someone is to urge or egg them on
Conference is a well-known British variety of pear

explanation.surface: Reporters end up with egg on their pears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg on' looks like a mess on fruit but means urge; Conference is a common British pear variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A press conference is an event at which reporters are briefed and put questions.
